narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To demonstrate that the monthly price of the cholesterol drug Crestor is higher in the United States than in other countries.

units.meaning: The US monthly price is the highest shown, at $230.946 per month.
accepted_routes: The US price is $230.946 per month.
The US monthly price is about $231.
United States: $230.95/month, the highest in the chart.
units.visual_evidence_rule: US bar must be visibly tallest and labeled or annotated with ~$230.946 (or rounded $231).
units.temporal_anchor: During or around the 'More expensive in the US' clause.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video state the exact US value, or is 'US is highest' enough?

units.meaning: The US price exceeds every other listed country; against the next-highest country, Germany, the gap is $193.1568.

basis.note: Highest non-US country in the table

accepted_routes: US costs more than all other countries shown.
US is higher than Germany, Canada, UK, France, Norway, and Australia.
US is $193.16 more than Germany, the next-highest country.
units.visual_evidence_rule: All non-US bars must be shorter than the US bar; if the gap is claimed, Germany should be highlighted as next highest or a gap annotation should be visible.
units.temporal_anchor: During the 'More expensive in the US' comparison.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly compare US to all other countries, or is comparison to Germany enough?

units.meaning: US price is a multiple of each other country: 6.11x Germany, 7.13x Canada, 8.81x UK, 11.52x France, 11.52x Norway, and 29.95x Australia.
accepted_routes: US is over 7 times Canada and nearly 30 times Australia.
The US price is 11.5 times France and Norway.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Ratio annotations or on-screen text must tie to specific country bars; at least the largest contrast, such as US vs Australia or Germany, should be visible if this unit is included.
units.temporal_anchor: During the US-abroad comparison after 'More expensive in the US'.
units.reviewer_question: Are ratio multiples required evidence or optional emphasis?

units.meaning: Among non-US countries, the order is Germany ($37.7892) > Canada ($32.3907) > United Kingdom ($26.2211) > France/Norway tied ($20.0514 each) > Australia ($7.71208).
accepted_routes: Germany is the most expensive non-US country, followed by Canada and the UK.
France and Norway are tied at $20.05, and Australia is lowest at $7.71.
The non-US ranking runs Germany, Canada, UK, France/Norway, Australia.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Non-US bars should be sorted descending or annotated so the ranking is readable.
units.temporal_anchor: Optional supporting detail during or after the 'More expensive in the US' clause.
units.reviewer_question: Is non-US ranking required, or acceptable to show only US-vs-all?

units.meaning: Other countries' prices are small shares of the US price: Germany 16.36%, Canada 14.03%, UK 11.35%, France/Norway 8.68%, Australia 3.34%.
accepted_routes: Germany pays about 16.4% of the US price.
Canada is about 14% of US price.
Australia is only about 3.3% of the US price.
Non-US prices range from 3.34% to 16.36% of the US price.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Percent-of-US labels or proportional bar scale must make the small shares visible; Germany and Australia should be directly comparable to the US.
units.temporal_anchor: During the comparison to the US, after 'More expensive in the US'.
units.reviewer_question: Are percent-of-US shares required or optional supporting detail?

optional_valid: Exact values for all seven countries can be displayed as labels.
US can be visually highlighted by color to emphasize its highest price.
Rounding the US price to $231 or other country values to two decimals is acceptable.
Relative values can be shown as percentages of US price rather than as raw dollars.
unsupported_to_avoid: Do not claim why the US price is higher, such as insurance, patents, or regulation, from this table.
Do not generalize to all cholesterol drugs or to countries not listed.
Do not call relative_value 'market share' or use population-adjusted prices; no such data.
Do not infer a time trend or future change; the table is a single monthly price comparison.
Do not use an unlisted average as the benchmark unless explicitly labeled as a simple average of the listed countries.
notes: Core required units are the US endpoint and US-vs-others comparison; ranking, ratios, and percent-of-US shares are defensible optional additions. Avoid causal or generalization claims.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
